newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's dinar tumbles, prices soar.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's dinar tumbles, prices soar.

text.p: Iraq's dinar is falling and prices of essential commodities rising, exacerbating life for millions of Iraqis striving to make ends meet under crippling U.N. trade sanctions.
The dinar on Sunday sank to about 1,640 to the U.S. dollar from 1,250 last week.
Traders said the slump was mainly caused by the revival of trade with Kurdish areas and removal of curbs on the circulation of many foreign goods.
Iraq this month lifted restrictions on travel and trade with its Kurdish north following the triumph of a Kurdish faction it backed in fighting with a rival Kurdish group.

The traders said business with Kurdish provinces, previously under a stiff internal blockade, was brisk and demand for foreign and local goods coming from the Kurdish north high in other parts of the country.
Iraqi shoppers gazed with astonishment at price labels in Baghdad's Shourja, Iraq's commercial hub.

A kg (2.2 lb) of flour started at 400 dinars in the morning and jumped to 500 in the afternoon. A tray of 30 eggs, worth 2,500 dinars last week, jumped to 3,250 on Sunday and a kg of cooking oil climbed to 2,000 dinars from 1,250.
Some traders said they expected the dinar to fall further as demand increased for foreign goods that the trade ministsry removed from its list of banned items.
Baghdad shops brimmed with foreign chocolates, sweets, juices and beverages. Foreign cigarettes were also being sold.
The dinar had made spectacular gains earlier this year when Iraq and the United Nations agreed to enter into serious talks on applying the oil-for-food scheme.
The dinar rose dramatically on the signing of the deal on May 20 and for a short period was trading at about 450 to the U.S. dollar. In January a dollar was worth about 3,000 dinars.
